id: title:ablaszkiewicz:deprecate event release mode on the mobile uploads

review.posthog_relevance: Changes the PostHog CLI and server-side symbol upload workflow to enforce release binding, removing the ability to upload symbol sets without an associated release. This could affect users uploading debug symbols for exception symbolication and release attribution.
review.reason: The observed changes remove the release-independent symbol upload option and add a deprecation warning, while retaining compatibility. This is a substantive, bounded change to the CLI and server-side symbol handling. observations.behavior: Adds a deprecation warning and removes the release-independent release binding, while retaining the flag for compatibility.
observations.posthog_connection: The CLI no longer allows symbol sets to be uploaded without release binding; the server will always associate the uploaded symbol set with the release created by the build. This preserves the release context needed for exception symbolication and release attribution. The warning helps users migrate away from the deprecated flag.

observations.behavior: Removes the conditional release-independent binding, always binding the uploaded symbol set to the release.
observations.posthog_connection: The upload implementation no longer distinguishes between release-bound and release-independent symbol sets; it always binds the symbol set to the release. This ensures that exceptions symbolicated against this mapping will have release attribution, and that the release context is preserved for the server-side event processing.
